name: dlm_midcomms_version_wait
prose: Precondition: the midcomms node hash (node_hash, protected by nodes_srcu) is initialised; the caller is not inside an nodes_srcu read-side section that would conflict and holds no lock the waits could depend on. Postcondition: returns void. Under srcu_read_lock(&nodes_srcu) it visits every node in node_hash and, for each node, sleeps on node->shutdown_wait for at most DLM_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT until node->version != DLM_VERSION_NOT_SET, or node->state == DLM_CLOSED, or DLM_NODE_FLAG_CLOSE is set in node->flags; if that wait timed out or the CLOSE flag is set a debug message is logged (never an error). It therefore may block for up to DLM_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT per node, does not modify any node, and releases the srcu read lock before returning.
note: Clarified: per-node wait, CLOSE flag also ends wait; node state is not modified.

name: midcomms_shutdown
prose: Precondition: node points to a valid midcomms_node that stays allocated for the call (e.g. under nodes_srcu); the caller does not hold node->state_lock. Postcondition: returns void. If node->version is not DLM_VERSION_3_2 (old protocol) it returns immediately without waiting or changing anything. Otherwise, under node->state_lock (bh-disabled spinlock, released before waiting): if node->state is DLM_ESTABLISHED it is changed to DLM_FIN_WAIT1 and a FIN is sent with dlm_send_fin(node, dlm_act_fin_ack_rcv); if the state is DLM_CLOSED nothing is done; in any other state it is left unchanged (the passive side completes the shutdown). It then (after an optional 5 s debug delay when DLM_DEBUG_FENCE_TERMINATION is set) waits on node->shutdown_wait for at most DLM_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT until node->state == DLM_CLOSED or DLM_NODE_FLAG_CLOSE is set, logs whether it timed out or completed, and returns either way without reporting an error.
note: Clarified lock scope (released before wait) and non-3.2 early return.

name: dlm_midcomms_close
prose: Precondition: nodeid is any integer node id; the caller holds neither close_lock nor nodes_srcu (the function calls synchronize_srcu(&nodes_srcu), which would deadlock inside a read-side section) and may sleep. Postcondition: returns the value of dlm_lowcomms_close(nodeid) (0 on success or a negative errno). If a midcomms node exists for nodeid it first sets DLM_NODE_FLAG_CLOSE on it and wakes its shutdown_wait waiters, then waits for an SRCU grace period, takes close_lock, and (re-looking the node up) calls dlm_lowcomms_close(nodeid), deletes the node's debugfs comms file, unlinks the node from the node hash under nodes_lock, waits for another SRCU grace period so no reader remains, drops all pending messages with dlm_send_queue_flush(node), and schedules the node to be freed with call_srcu(midcomms_node_release); the caller must not use the node afterwards. If no node exists (at the first or at the second lookup) only dlm_lowcomms_close(nodeid) is performed and its value returned. close_lock and the srcu read lock are released on every path before returning.
note: Added the no-SRCU-reader-section precondition; ret is dlm_lowcomms_close's value in both paths.

name: recover_master
prose: Precondition: r is a valid rsb with a valid lockspace r->res_ls, count points to a writable unsigned int, seq is the recovery sequence number; the caller holds the locks required to modify the rsb during recovery (this function takes ls_recover_xa_lock itself, via recover_xa_add). Postcondition: if r->res_nodeid != -1 and we are already the master (is_master(r)), or the master is not a removed node and RSB_NEW_MASTER is not set (this includes res_nodeid == -1 with RSB_NEW_MASTER clear), it returns 0 without changing r or *count. Otherwise it always increments *count by one and then: if we are the directory node for r (dlm_dir_nodeid(r) == dlm_our_nodeid()) it, when the old master was removed, sets r->res_master_nodeid to our nodeid and r->res_nodeid to 0, calls set_new_master(r) (sets the master of the rsb's lkbs and the RSB_NEW_MASTER and RSB_NEW_MASTER2 flags) and returns 0; otherwise it calls recover_xa_add(r), ignoring its result (on success the rsb is registered on the recover xarray with one extra reference held until recover_xa_del/clear, and res_id set; if r is already registered or allocation fails it is not added again), and returns the result of dlm_send_rcom_lookup(r, dir_nodeid, seq): 0 on success or a negative errno.
note: Fixed round-2 issue: early return 0 when res_nodeid == -1 and RSB_NEW_MASTER not set (count unchanged).

name: to_dlm_errno
prose: Precondition: none; err is any int (callers pass 0 or a negative errno). Postcondition: returns -DLM_ERRNO_X when err is -X for X in EDEADLK, EBADR, EBADSLT, EPROTO, EOPNOTSUPP, ETIMEDOUT or EINPROGRESS (the local errno is translated to the fixed DLM wire value; DLM_ERRNO_* are 35, 53, 57, 71, 95, 110 and 115), and returns err unchanged for every other value, including 0 and positive values. Pure: no memory, locks or references.
note: Previous contract assumed local errno numbers equal wire numbers and required err <= 0; now exact switch mapping for all int inputs.

name: from_dlm_errno
prose: Precondition: none; err is any int (typically 0 or a negated DLM wire errno). Postcondition: returns -X (the local errno) when err is -DLM_ERRNO_X for X in EDEADLK, EBADR, EBADSLT, EPROTO, EOPNOTSUPP, ETIMEDOUT or EINPROGRESS (wire values 35, 53, 57, 71, 95, 110 and 115), and returns err unchanged for every other value, including 0 and positive values. Pure: no memory, locks or references.
note: Exact switch mapping for all int inputs, using the macro names.

name: static inline void ecryptfs_release_messaging(void)
prose: This is the static inline stub used when CONFIG_ECRYPT_FS_MESSAGING is not enabled (the same header declares only the prototype of the real function, implemented in messaging.c, when it is enabled). Precondition: none (no parameters). Postcondition: the stub body is empty: it returns nothing, performs no action, and acquires or releases no lock, reference or memory.
note: The slice shows a real (empty) inline stub in the #else branch, so it is fixed, not dropped; name given as the definition head from the slice.

name: process_find_global_auth_tok_for_sig_err
prose: Precondition: none; err_code is any int (callers pass a negated errno). Postcondition: returns err_code unchanged when it is -ENOENT or -EINVAL (after logging a 'Missing auth tok' or 'Invalid auth tok' warning); otherwise it returns process_request_key_err(err_code), i.e. -ENOENT for -ENOKEY, -ETIME for -EKEYEXPIRED, and -EINVAL for -EKEYREVOKED and for every other value (including 0 and positive values), each with a warning logged. No memory, locks or references are touched; only logging happens as a side effect.
note: Contract rewritten with macro names and valid for all int inputs; the callee process_request_key_err is inlined into the ensures.

name: parse_tag_3_packet
prose: Real function parse_tag_3_packet(crypt_stat, data, auth_tok_list, new_auth_tok, packet_size, max_packet_size); the slice cuts its head, so the name is not in the slice. Precondition: data points to at least max_packet_size readable bytes, max_packet_size being the number of bytes available for the packet; crypt_stat is the caller's crypt_stat; auth_tok_list is a list owned by the caller; new_auth_tok and packet_size point to writable storage. Postcondition: first sets *packet_size = 0 and *new_auth_tok = NULL. On success returns 0, having allocated an auth_tok_list_item, filled it from the packet (salt, hash iterations computed from the RFC 2440 count byte, the encrypted session key and its size, token_type ECRYPTFS_PASSWORD with hash_algo 0x01 MD5, flags ECRYPTFS_CONTAINS_ENCRYPTED_KEY set and the decrypted-key and userspace-try flags cleared), added it at the head of auth_tok_list (the caller later frees it via wipe_auth_tok_list), set *new_auth_tok to point at its auth_tok, set crypt_stat->cipher (via ecryptfs_cipher_code_to_string) and crypt_stat->key_size (24 for the AES-192 cipher code, else the encrypted key size), initialised crypt_stat's crypto context, and set *packet_size to the number of bytes consumed. On failure it returns a negative errno with *new_auth_tok = NULL and *packet_size = 0 and no list item left allocated (a partially filled item is zeroed and freed): -EINVAL if max_packet_size < ECRYPTFS_SALT_SIZE + 7, the first byte is not ECRYPTFS_TAG_3_PACKET_TYPE, the body size is below ECRYPTFS_SALT_SIZE + 5 or the packet exceeds max_packet_size, the encrypted key is larger than ECRYPTFS_MAX_KEY_BYTES, or the version byte is not 0x04; -ENOMEM if the item cannot be allocated; -ENOSYS for an S2K specifier other than 3 or a hash id other than 0x01; or the error from ecryptfs_parse_packet_length, ecryptfs_cipher_code_to_string or ecryptfs_init_crypt_ctx. On failure crypt_stat->cipher/key_size may already have been modified.
note: Slice head cut; name added. Noted that crypt_stat may be partially modified on late failures.

name: ecryptfs_parse_param
prose: Real function ecryptfs_parse_param(fc, param); the slice cuts its head, so the name is not in the slice. Precondition: fc is a valid eCryptfs fs_context whose fc->fs_private (struct ecryptfs_fs_context) and fc->s_fs_info (struct ecryptfs_sb_info) are set, and param is a parsed mount parameter whose string value (for string options) is NUL-terminated. Postcondition: returns the negative error of fs_parse if param does not match the option spec; otherwise applies the option and returns 0, or returns -EINVAL for an option that is in the spec but not handled. Per option: sig/ecryptfs_sig registers the signature with ecryptfs_add_global_auth_tok (its error is returned, ctx->sig_set unset) and sets ctx->sig_set; cipher/ecryptfs_cipher copies the name (strscpy) into mount_crypt_stat->global_default_cipher_name and sets ctx->cipher_name_set; ecryptfs_key_bytes stores the 32-bit value in global_default_cipher_key_size and sets ctx->cipher_key_bytes_set; passthrough, xattr_metadata, encrypted_view (which also sets XATTR_METADATA), unlink_sigs and mount_auth_tok_only OR the corresponding ECRYPTFS_* flags into mount_crypt_stat->flags; fnek_sig first copies the signature into global_default_fnek_sig, then registers it as an FNEK auth tok (on failure returns its error leaving the copied string and flags unset), then sets ECRYPTFS_GLOBAL_ENCRYPT_FILENAMES | ECRYPTFS_GLOBAL_ENCFN_USE_MOUNT_FNEK; fn_cipher copies the name and sets ctx->fn_cipher_name_set; fn_cipher_key_bytes stores the 32-bit value and sets ctx->fn_cipher_key_bytes_set; check_dev_ruid sets ctx->check_ruid. A successful sig registration allocates a global auth tok attached to mount_crypt_stat. No locks are taken by this function itself.
note: Slice head cut; per-option behaviour enumerated.

name: ecryptfs_get_tree
prose: Precondition: fc is a valid eCryptfs fs_context with fc->fs_private (ecryptfs_fs_context) and fc->s_fs_info (ecryptfs_sb_info sbi) set; fc->source may be NULL. Postcondition: returns 0 on success with fc->root set to a new reference to the root dentry of a freshly created anonymous superblock (ops, xattr handlers and dentry ops installed, lower superblock/dentry/mount recorded, flags: POSIXACL copied from the lower fs, SB_RDONLY forced if the lower fs is read-only or the encrypted view is enabled, stack depth = lower depth + 1, SB_ACTIVE set), the sbi owned by that superblock, and the lower path reference kept in the superblock private data. On failure it returns a negative errno and logs it: -EINVAL if fc->source is NULL, ecryptfs_validate_options fails (its error), the lower directory is on an eCryptfs mount or on an idmapped mount, or the stacking depth would exceed FILESYSTEM_MAX_STACK_DEPTH; -EPERM if ctx->check_ruid is set and the lower directory is not owned by the current uid; -ENOMEM if d_make_root fails; or the error of sget_fc, super_setup_bdi, kern_path or ecryptfs_get_inode. Ownership of sbi: before ecryptfs_set_superblock_private succeeds (failures of the NULL-source check, option validation, sget_fc and super_setup_bdi) sbi stays with the fs_context and its mount_crypt_stat is destroyed here via ecryptfs_destroy_mount_crypt_stat when sbi is still set; after it has been attached, sbi is owned by the superblock and freed by its kill_sb. On failures after the superblock exists, the lower path reference is dropped (when kern_path succeeded) and the superblock is deactivated with deactivate_locked_super.
note: Corrected ownership: sbi destroyed here on failures before attach (mount_crypt_stat), owned by the sb afterwards.

name: ecryptfs_miscdev_open
prose: Precondition: inode and file are the misc device inode and the file being opened; the caller holds neither ecryptfs_daemon_hash_mux nor any daemon->mux. Postcondition: takes ecryptfs_daemon_hash_mux and releases it before returning on every path. It looks up a daemon for the caller's euid with ecryptfs_find_daemon_by_euid: if one already exists (open or not) it returns -EINVAL with nothing changed. Otherwise it spawns a daemon with ecryptfs_spawn_daemon (if that fails it logs and returns its negative errno; the daemon mutex has not been taken). On success of the spawn it takes daemon->mux; if the daemon already has ECRYPTFS_DAEMON_MISCDEV_OPEN set it returns -EBUSY, otherwise it sets that flag, stores the daemon in file->private_data, increments ecryptfs_num_miscdev_opens and returns 0; daemon->mux is released on both of those paths.
note: Fixed: existing daemon of any kind gives -EINVAL; daemon->mux only taken after successful spawn.

name: erofs_inode_is_data_compressed
prose: Precondition: none; datamode is any unsigned int (the valid EROFS datalayout values are EROFS_INODE_FLAT_PLAIN=0, EROFS_INODE_COMPRESSED_FULL=1, EROFS_INODE_FLAT_INLINE=2, EROFS_INODE_COMPRESSED_COMPACT=3 and EROFS_INODE_CHUNK_BASED=4, but the function does not check the range). Postcondition: returns true exactly when datamode equals EROFS_INODE_COMPRESSED_COMPACT (3) or EROFS_INODE_COMPRESSED_FULL (1), and false for every other value including values above 4. Pure: no memory, locks or references.
contract: /*@ requires 1; ensures result == (datamode == EROFS_INODE_COMPRESSED_COMPACT || datamode == EROFS_INODE_COMPRESSED_FULL); */
note: Precondition datamode<=4 dropped (the code compares for any unsigned value).

name: reverse_path_check
prose: Precondition: the caller holds the epoll global locks (epnested_mutex) that protect tfile_check_list; tfile_check_list is a singly linked list of struct epitems_head terminated by EP_UNACTIVE_PTR (not NULL; EP_UNACTIVE_PTR means an empty list); path_count and path_limits are the static path-counting arrays. Postcondition: for each entry in tfile_check_list in order it resets all path_count[] entries to 0 (path_count_init), then under rcu_read_lock runs reverse_path_check_proc on the entry's epitems starting at depth 0 and releases the RCU read lock; if that returns a non-zero value (which is always -1: nesting deeper than EP_MAX_NESTS or a path count exceeding path_limits) the function returns that value immediately and the remaining entries are not checked. It returns 0 if every entry passes or the list is empty. The RCU read lock is never held on return and nothing is modified except the path_count array.
note: Fixed: list is EP_UNACTIVE_PTR-terminated; error is -1; caller holds epnested_mutex.

name: ep_modify
prose: Precondition: ep->mtx is held, IRQs are enabled, epi is an epitem registered in ep whose target file the caller holds a reference to, and event points to a valid epoll_event. Postcondition: always returns 0 (no error is reported). epi->event.events and epi->event.data are overwritten from *event; if EPOLLWAKEUP is set in the new events and epi has no wakeup source, ep_create_wakeup_source is attempted but its failure (-ENOMEM) is ignored, so epi may still have no wakeup source; if EPOLLWAKEUP is clear and epi has one, it is destroyed. After a full memory barrier epi's file is polled with the new mask: if it reports ready events, then under ep->lock (spin_lock_irq) and only if epi is not already linked on the ready list, epi is appended to ep->rdllist, ep_pm_stay_awake is called, ep->wq waiters are woken and, if ep->poll_wait has waiters, ep_poll_safewake is called after dropping the lock. If epi is already on the ready list it stays there unchanged, and if the poll reports no ready events the ready-list state is left unchanged (an already-linked epi is not removed). No reference is acquired or released.
note: Fixed: wakeup source creation may silently fail; an already-linked item stays linked.

name: begin_new_exec
prose: Precondition: called by a binfmt handler's load_binary for the current task with bprm prepared (bprm->cred holding the prepared new credentials, bprm->mm the new, not yet installed mm, bprm->file the binary); the caller holds current->signal->cred_guard_mutex (taken when the exec was set up) and does NOT hold exec_update_lock, which exec_mmap acquires inside this function. Postcondition: returns 0 or a negative errno. On success the point of no return has been passed, the old mm replaced by bprm->mm (bprm->mm set to NULL), the new credentials committed with commit_creds (bprm->cred set to NULL, ownership passed to the task), signal handlers, files table (close-on-exec applied) and task namespaces reset, the task comm set and the task made the only thread; if bprm->have_execfd a new fd for bprm->executable is installed and stored in bprm->execfd (bprm->executable set to NULL); the function returns with both exec_update_lock (write) and cred_guard_mutex still held, to be released later by setup_new_exec/the caller. On failure it returns the negative errno of the failing step (from bprm_creds_from_file, de_thread, unshare_files, set_mm_exe_file, exec_mmap, exec_task_namespaces, unshare_sighand, set_cred_ucounts or get_unused_fd_flags; e.g. -EINTR, -ENOMEM, -EMFILE): for failures before exec_mmap succeeds (including bprm_creds_from_file) exec_update_lock is not held and cred_guard_mutex stays held with bprm->cred still allocated (the caller's cleanup frees it and unlocks); for failures after exec_mmap succeeded exec_update_lock is released, and cred_guard_mutex is released only if the credentials had already been committed (bprm->cred == NULL), otherwise it stays held. Once bprm->point_of_no_return is set (every failure after bprm_creds_from_file) the caller treats the error as fatal to the task.
note: Fixed per round-2: exec_update_lock is taken by exec_mmap inside; caller holds only cred_guard_mutex; lock state per failure stage.

name: bprm_fill_uid
prose: Precondition: bprm is a valid linux_binprm with bprm->cred pointing to the prepared (not yet committed) credentials, and file is the binary's open struct file with a valid inode; the caller holds no inode lock of file's inode. Postcondition: returns void and never fails. It does nothing (bprm unchanged) if the file's mount forbids suid (mnt_may_suid false), if the current task has no_new_privs set, if the inode's mode has neither S_ISUID nor S_ISGID, if after taking and dropping the inode lock (to reload mode/uid/gid consistently, with inode_permission(MAY_EXEC) evaluated under the lock) the exec permission check failed, or if the file's uid or gid has no mapping in bprm->cred->user_ns. Otherwise: if the reloaded mode has S_ISUID then bprm->per_clear gains PER_CLEAR_ON_SETID and bprm->cred->euid is set to the file's owner (mapped to a kuid); and if the mode has both S_ISGID and S_IXGRP then bprm->per_clear gains PER_CLEAR_ON_SETID and bprm->cred->egid is set to the file's group. S_ISGID without the group-exec bit changes nothing. Only bprm->per_clear and bprm->cred->euid/egid are modified (not other credential or capability fields). The inode lock is taken and released internally; no reference is retained.
note: Fixed: S_ISGID alone (without S_IXGRP) has no effect; per_clear is set only on the S_ISUID and S_ISGID+S_IXGRP paths.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE3(execve
prose: Generated function sys_execve(filename, argv, envp) (the macro SYSCALL_DEFINE3(execve, ...) defines it). Precondition: filename is a user pointer to a NUL-terminated path, argv and envp are user pointers to NULL-terminated arrays of user string pointers (either may be NULL meaning empty); the caller is the current task in process context. Postcondition: copies the path with getname and returns do_execve(...) i.e. do_execveat_common(AT_FDCWD, name, argv, envp, 0): on success the current process image is replaced and the syscall returns 0 into the new program; on failure it returns a negative errno (the getname error such as -EFAULT, -ENAMETOOLONG, -ENOENT or -ENOMEM; -EAGAIN if RLIMIT_NPROC is exceeded; -E2BIG or -EFAULT from argument counting/copying; -ENOEXEC, -EACCES, -ENOENT and other errors from loading) and the old image continues. The struct filename obtained from getname is always consumed (released with putname) inside do_execveat_common, so nothing is leaked; no locks are held on return.
note: Macro-generated function: the real function name (sys_execve) does not occur literally in the source, so the name field is the macro invocation head from the slice.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE5(execveat
prose: Generated function sys_execveat(fd, filename, argv, envp, flags) (defined by SYSCALL_DEFINE5(execveat, ...)). Precondition: fd is a directory file descriptor or AT_FDCWD (or, with AT_EMPTY_PATH, an executable file descriptor), filename is a user pointer to a path string, argv and envp are user pointers to NULL-terminated arrays of user string pointers, and flags is a combination of AT_EMPTY_PATH and AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW. Postcondition: copies the path with getname_uflags(filename, flags) (which permits an empty path under AT_EMPTY_PATH) and returns do_execveat(fd, name, argv, envp, flags), i.e. do_execveat_common: 0 into the new program image on success, otherwise a negative errno (getname errors, -EINVAL for unsupported flags, -EAGAIN for RLIMIT_NPROC, -E2BIG/-EFAULT for argument problems, errors from opening or loading the binary such as -ENOENT, -EACCES, -ENOEXEC, -EBADF). The struct filename is always consumed inside do_execveat_common; no locks are held on return.
note: Macro-generated function: real name sys_execveat is not literally in the source; the name field is the macro invocation head.

name: COMPAT_SYSCALL_DEFINE3(execve
prose: Generated function compat_sys_execve(filename, argv, envp) (defined by COMPAT_SYSCALL_DEFINE3(execve, ...), only with CONFIG_COMPAT). Precondition: filename is a user pointer to a NUL-terminated path; argv and envp are user pointers to NULL-terminated arrays of 32-bit compat user pointers. Postcondition: copies the path with getname and returns compat_do_execve(...), i.e. do_execveat_common(AT_FDCWD, name, compat argv, compat envp, 0): 0 into the new image on success, or a negative errno with the old image continuing (getname error, -EAGAIN, -E2BIG, -EFAULT, loader errors such as -ENOENT, -EACCES, -ENOEXEC). The struct filename is always consumed inside do_execveat_common; no locks are held on return.
note: Macro-generated function: real name compat_sys_execve is not literally in the source; name is the macro invocation head.

name: COMPAT_SYSCALL_DEFINE5(execveat
prose: Generated function compat_sys_execveat(fd, filename, argv, envp, flags) (defined by COMPAT_SYSCALL_DEFINE5(execveat, ...), only with CONFIG_COMPAT). Precondition: fd is a directory descriptor or AT_FDCWD (or an executable fd with AT_EMPTY_PATH), filename a user path pointer, argv and envp are user pointers to NULL-terminated arrays of 32-bit compat user pointers, and flags a combination of AT_EMPTY_PATH and AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW. Postcondition: copies the path with getname_uflags(filename, flags) and returns compat_do_execveat(fd, name, argv, envp, flags), i.e. do_execveat_common with compat argument arrays: 0 into the new image on success, otherwise a negative errno (getname error, -EINVAL for bad flags, -EAGAIN, -E2BIG, -EFAULT, -EBADF, loader errors). The struct filename is always consumed inside do_execveat_common; no locks are held on return.
note: Macro-generated function, wrongly dropped before; name is the macro invocation head (without the closing parenthesis) as it appears in the slice.

name: de_thread
prose: Precondition: tsk is the current task, about to complete an exec, and tsk->signal and tsk->sighand are valid; the caller holds no siglock or tasklist_lock and may sleep. Postcondition: returns 0 or -EAGAIN. If the thread group has only tsk (thread_group_empty) it just sets tsk->exit_signal = SIGCHLD and returns 0. Otherwise, under the sighand siglock: if the group is already exiting (SIGNAL_GROUP_EXIT) or another task is already exec-ing (sig->group_exec_task non-NULL) it returns -EAGAIN with no state changed; else it sets sig->group_exec_task = tsk, kills all other threads (zap_other_threads) and sleeps killably until they have exited (notify_count reaches 0). If a fatal signal becomes pending during either wait (waiting for the other threads, or for the old leader to become a zombie) it takes tasklist_lock for reading, resets sig->group_exec_task = NULL and sig->notify_count = 0, and returns -EAGAIN (the state it set is unwound; other threads may already have been killed). If tsk was not the group leader it waits for the old leader to exit, then under tasklist_lock (write) and the cgroup threadgroup lock it takes over the leader's start_time/start_boottime, swaps tids with it (exchange_tids), transfers its TGID, PGID and SID pids, replaces it in the tasks/sibling lists, becomes the group leader with exit_signal SIGCHLD, marks the old leader EXIT_DEAD and releases it with release_task(). On success it resets sig->group_exec_task = NULL and sig->notify_count = 0, sets tsk->exit_signal = SIGCHLD, and returns 0 with tsk the sole thread and group leader and no lock held.
note: Fixed per round-2: the fatal-signal path does unwind group_exec_task/notify_count (code at label killed); the group-exit/exec-in-progress -EAGAIN returns with no change.

name: exfat_get_cluster
prose: Real function exfat_get_cluster(inode, cluster, fclus, dclus, last_dclus, allow_eof) (the packet name exfat_find_last_cluster does not exist in the source and the slice cuts the function head). Precondition: inode is a valid exfat inode, cluster is the file-relative cluster index to locate, fclus, dclus and last_dclus point to writable unsigned ints, and allow_eof is non-zero if reaching the end of the chain at or before cluster is acceptable; the caller holds the filesystem lock as usual for exfat chain walks. Postcondition: returns 0 or -EIO. If ei->start_clu is EXFAT_FREE_CLUSTER it reports a filesystem error and returns -EIO with the output variables untouched. Otherwise it sets *fclus = 0 and *dclus = *last_dclus = ei->start_clu; if cluster == 0 or ei->start_clu == EXFAT_EOF_CLUSTER it returns 0 without using the cache. Otherwise it looks up the nearest cached position with exfat_cache_lookup (updating *fclus/*dclus), returns 0 at once (without exfat_cache_add) if *fclus == cluster, and else walks the FAT chain with exfat_ent_get, updating *last_dclus to the previous cluster, *dclus to the next one and incrementing *fclus per step. It returns -EIO when *fclus exceeds the filesystem's cluster count (chain loop, reported as a fs error), when exfat_ent_get fails, or when the chain reaches EXFAT_EOF_CLUSTER and allow_eof is zero (reported as a fs error), in each case without calling exfat_cache_add and leaving the outputs at the partial-walk values. On success it records the traversed run with exfat_cache_add and returns 0 with *fclus == cluster and *dclus the cluster's number and *last_dclus the preceding cluster's number, or (allow_eof) with *dclus == EXFAT_EOF_CLUSTER, *last_dclus the last valid cluster and *fclus <= cluster.
note: Real function is exfat_get_cluster (packet name does not exist in the source); head cut; added the EXFAT_FREE_CLUSTER -EIO path.

name: exfat_get_block
prose: Precondition: inode is a valid exfat inode, bh_result is a buffer_head whose b_size is the requested mapping length in bytes (a positive multiple of the block size) and whose b_folio may be NULL (direct I/O), iblock is the file-relative block, create is 0 or 1, and the caller does not hold sbi->s_lock (taken and released exactly once here). Postcondition: returns 0 or a negative errno. If iblock >= last_block (i_size rounded up) and !create, or the cluster lookup yields EXFAT_EOF_CLUSTER, it jumps to the common exit: returns 0 with b_size set to the byte size of the original max_blocks (the caller's requested length) and the buffer not mapped. If exfat_map_cluster fails it returns that errno (including -ENOSPC) at once, with bh_result (b_size and flags) untouched. Otherwise the block is mapped with map_bh (clearing any delay flag) and max_blocks is limited to the rest of the cluster; then, depending on ei->valid_size: a range fully below valid_size is mapped as is; a range straddling it is shortened to the written part; for create beyond valid_size the buffer is also marked new, ei->valid_size is advanced to cover the range and the inode is marked dirty; for a non-create access wholly beyond valid_size the mapped flag is cleared (zero fill later); for a read of the single block partly beyond valid_size (iblock == valid_blks, folio-backed) the block count becomes 1 and: -EAGAIN if the folio has no buffers, -EINVAL (with a fs error message) if b_data does not match the folio address, the error of bh_read if reading fails, otherwise the block is read and its unwritten tail zeroed (0). At the common exit b_size is set to max_blocks blocks in bytes, and if the result is negative the mapped flag is cleared (so on the -EAGAIN, -EINVAL and bh_read-error paths b_size is set and the buffer unmapped). b_size is bounded by the cluster boundary and the caller's size and, in the partially-written and fully-beyond-valid_size cases, is not further reduced to valid_size.
note: Fixed per round-1/2: exfat_map_cluster failure leaves bh_result untouched; b_size not bounded by valid_size beyond it.

name: init_exfat_fs
prose: Precondition: called once from module initialisation (init_exfat_fs, __init) with no parameters, before any exfat mount; exfat_inode_cachep is not yet created and exfat_fs_type is not yet registered. Postcondition: returns 0 with the exfat cache subsystem initialised (exfat_cache_init), the 'exfat_inode_cache' slab (struct exfat_inode_info objects, SLAB_RECLAIM_ACCOUNT, constructor exfat_inode_init_once) stored in exfat_inode_cachep, and the exfat file_system_type registered with register_filesystem. On failure returns a negative errno and leaves nothing behind: the error of exfat_cache_init (nothing was created); -ENOMEM if kmem_cache_create fails (after exfat_cache_shutdown); or the error of register_filesystem (after kmem_cache_destroy of the inode cache and exfat_cache_shutdown). No locks or references are retained.
note: Prose already correct; the old contract only constrained the sign and described the wrong function (exfat_init_fs_context) per reviewers, so removed (function has no parameters and touches global state).

name: ext2_init_acl
prose: Real function ext2_init_acl(inode, dir); the slice cuts the head so the name is not in the slice. Precondition: inode is a newly created inode whose i_mode is initialised and whose i_acl and i_default_acl have not yet been set, and dir is the parent directory from which default ACLs are inherited. Postcondition: returns 0 or a negative errno. It calls posix_acl_create(dir, &inode->i_mode, &default_acl, &acl), which may modify inode->i_mode (umask or ACL mask); if that fails its error is returned and nothing else is done. Otherwise: if default_acl is non-NULL it is installed with __ext2_set_acl(ACL_TYPE_DEFAULT) and the reference is released, else inode->i_default_acl is set to NULL; if acl is non-NULL the access ACL is installed with __ext2_set_acl(ACL_TYPE_ACCESS) only if the default ACL installation did not fail (the first error is kept) and its reference is released either way, else inode->i_acl is set to NULL. Both ACL references obtained from posix_acl_create are always released, so the caller gains no references; on failure the inode's cached ACL pointers may be left unset.
note: Slice head cut; prose largely confirmed, mode modification by posix_acl_create added.

name: ext2_set_link
prose: Precondition: dir is the directory inode, de points to a directory entry inside the mapped folio of dir (the caller holds a reference on the folio and the directory's i_rwsem as usual for directory modification), folio is that directory page, inode is the inode the entry should point at, and the caller does NOT hold the folio lock (it is taken here). Postcondition: returns 0 or a negative errno. It locks the folio and calls ext2_prepare_chunk for the entry's chunk: if that fails it unlocks the folio and returns its error, with the entry and dir unmodified. Otherwise it sets de->inode to inode->i_ino and the entry's file type from inode->i_mode, commits the chunk with ext2_commit_chunk (which unlocks the folio), and if update_times is true sets dir's mtime and ctime to the current time; it then clears EXT2_BTREE_FL in dir's ext2 flags, marks dir dirty, and returns the result of ext2_handle_dirsync(dir) (0, or a negative errno from the write-and-wait of a synchronous directory, in which case the entry has already been changed on disk cache). The folio is unlocked on return in every case, and the function neither takes nor releases the caller's folio reference.
note: Fixed per round-2: the folio lock is taken here, unlocked by prepare-failure path or commit; return is ext2_handle_dirsync's result.

name: ext2_fill_super
prose: Real function ext2_fill_super(sb, fc) (the slice cuts the head, so the name is not in the slice). Precondition: sb is a super_block with a block device (sb->s_bdev) and no s_fs_info yet; fc is the fs_context with fc->fs_private (struct ext2_fs_context with s_sb_block and mount options) and fc->sb_flags (SB_SILENT suppresses some diagnostics). Postcondition: returns 0 or a negative errno. On success it has allocated sbi (sb->s_fs_info) with its blockgroup lock, read and validated the ext2 superblock (keeping its buffer head in sbi->s_sbh and es in sbi->s_es), set the block size, applied the mount options and feature checks, allocated and read all group descriptor buffer heads (sbi->s_group_desc, sbi->s_debts), initialised the reservation window and the free-block, free-inode and directory percpu counters and the xattr cache, read the root inode and installed sb->s_root, warned if it is an ext3 filesystem, called ext2_setup_super (setting SB_RDONLY on sb if it reports a problem) and ext2_write_super. On failure it returns: -ENOMEM if sbi or its blockgroup lock cannot be allocated (before anything else is done) or for later allocation failures (descriptor array, debts array, root dentry, xattr cache); the error of the percpu counter init or of ext2_iget; and otherwise -EINVAL (unable to set the blocksize, unreadable superblock, bad magic, unsupported incompat or RO-incompat features, invalid log block size, bad inode size or group geometry, corrupt group descriptors or root inode). On every failure path it releases everything acquired so far (the superblock and descriptor buffer heads, the descriptor and debts arrays, percpu counters, xattr cache, the dax device reference, the blockgroup lock and sbi) and sets sb->s_fs_info = NULL (except for the very first -ENOMEM paths where it was never set). The root dentry/inode references stay owned by sb on success.
note: Slice head cut; prose rewritten with the error codes per stage.

name: ext2_quota_read
prose: Real function ext2_quota_read(sb, type, data, len, off) (the slice cuts the head, so only the body and a prototype reference exist). Precondition: sb is a mounted ext2 superblock with the quota file of the given type open (sb_dqopt(sb)->files[type] valid), data points to a writable buffer of at least len bytes, off is a byte offset in the quota file; no other task modifies the quota file (the quota layer serialises). Postcondition: returns 0 if off is greater than the quota file's i_size (it also returns 0 for off == i_size since the length is then clipped to 0); otherwise it clips len to i_size - off when off + len exceeds i_size and returns the clipped length after filling data[0 .. len) block by block: a block that ext2_get_block (read mode) reports as a hole (unmapped) is zero-filled, a mapped block is read with sb_bread and copied. On failure it returns a negative errno instead of a byte count: the error of ext2_get_block, or -EIO if sb_bread returns NULL; bytes of data already filled before the failure remain written but are not reported. No buffer head is held and no lock or reference is retained on any return path.
note: Slice head cut; added hole handling (zero fill) and the i_size clip details.

name: ext4_set_context
prose: Precondition: inode is an ext4 inode, ctx points to a valid fscrypt encryption context of len bytes, and fs_data is either NULL (set the context on an existing inode, in its own transaction) or a journal handle_t for a larger transaction creating a new inode (the inode already has the encrypt flag set and may not use inline data). Postcondition: returns 0 or a negative errno. Fails, changing nothing, with -EPERM if inode is the root inode, -EINVAL (with WARN_ON_ONCE) if S_DAX is set, -EOPNOTSUPP if the EXT4_INODE_DAX flag is set, or the error of ext4_convert_inline_data. If fs_data (handle) is non-NULL it additionally returns -EINVAL (with WARN_ON_ONCE) if the inode is not already IS_ENCRYPTED or still has EXT4_STATE_MAY_INLINE_DATA; otherwise it returns just the result of ext4_xattr_set_handle(handle, ..., ctx, len, XATTR_CREATE), without touching the ENCRYPT inode flag, S_ENCRYPTED or the inode's dirty state (the caller handles those). If fs_data is NULL it initialises dquot (its error returned), computes the xattr journal credits (error returned), starts its own journal handle (PTR_ERR of failure returned) and calls ext4_xattr_set_handle with flag 0; if that succeeds it sets EXT4_INODE_ENCRYPT, updates inode->i_flags (S_ENCRYPTED) and marks the inode dirty (a failure there is logged and returned), then stops the handle; if the xattr set failed with -ENOSPC and ext4_should_retry_alloc allows it, the whole transaction is retried; otherwise the result is the xattr/mark-dirty error, or, if those succeeded, the result of ext4_journal_stop. So with fs_data NULL a negative return can happen after the ENCRYPT flag was set (mark-dirty or journal-stop failure). The journal handle started here is always stopped before returning.
note: Fixed per round-2: with a handle the function only writes the xattr (XATTR_CREATE) and does not set flags; own-handle path sets ENCRYPT/S_ENCRYPTED.

name: EXT4_FEATURE_COMPAT_FUNCS(journal,		HAS_JOURNAL)
prose: Generated function ext4_has_feature_journal(sb) (one of the three inline functions that the macro invocation EXT4_FEATURE_COMPAT_FUNCS(journal, HAS_JOURNAL) defines). Precondition: sb is a valid ext4 super_block whose EXT4_SB(sb)->s_es on-disk superblock copy is valid and readable. Postcondition: returns true if and only if the EXT4_FEATURE_COMPAT_HAS_JOURNAL bit (0x0004) is set in s_es->s_feature_compat (compared after cpu_to_le32 conversion), otherwise false; it modifies no state and takes no lock.
note: Macro-generated function: the real name ext4_has_feature_journal does not occur literally in the slice; name is the exact macro invocation from the slice.

name: EXT4_FEATURE_COMPAT_FUNCS(journal,		HAS_JOURNAL)
prose: Generated function ext4_set_feature_journal(sb) (defined by the macro invocation EXT4_FEATURE_COMPAT_FUNCS(journal, HAS_JOURNAL)). Precondition: sb is a valid ext4 super_block whose EXT4_SB(sb)->s_es superblock copy is valid and writable. Postcondition: first calls ext4_update_dynamic_rev(sb) (which may raise s_es->s_rev_level to the dynamic revision and initialise the related fields), then ORs EXT4_FEATURE_COMPAT_HAS_JOURNAL (0x0004) into s_es->s_feature_compat leaving all other bits unchanged; returns nothing. It does not mark the superblock buffer dirty, takes no lock and no reference.
note: Macro-generated function: name is the exact macro invocation from the slice; real name ext4_set_feature_journal.

name: EXT4_FEATURE_COMPAT_FUNCS(journal,		HAS_JOURNAL)
prose: Generated function ext4_clear_feature_journal(sb) (defined by the macro invocation EXT4_FEATURE_COMPAT_FUNCS(journal, HAS_JOURNAL)). Precondition: sb is a valid ext4 super_block whose EXT4_SB(sb)->s_es superblock copy is valid and writable. Postcondition: clears the EXT4_FEATURE_COMPAT_HAS_JOURNAL bit (0x0004) in s_es->s_feature_compat, leaving all other bits unchanged; unlike the set function it does not call ext4_update_dynamic_rev; returns nothing, does not mark the superblock dirty, takes no lock and no reference.
note: Macro-generated function: name is the exact macro invocation from the slice; real name ext4_clear_feature_journal.

name: EXTN_FEATURE_FUNCS(4)
prose: Generated function ext4_has_unknown_ext4_incompat_features(sb) (one of three inline functions defined by the macro invocation EXTN_FEATURE_FUNCS(4), with ver = 4). Precondition: sb is a valid ext4 super_block whose EXT4_SB(sb)->s_es superblock copy is valid and readable. Postcondition: returns true if and only if s_es->s_feature_incompat has at least one bit set outside EXT4_FEATURE_INCOMPAT_SUPP (the mask of incompat features this kernel supports; the test is (s_feature_incompat & cpu_to_le32(~EXT4_FEATURE_INCOMPAT_SUPP)) != 0), otherwise false; it modifies no state and takes no lock.
note: Macro-generated function: name is the macro invocation from the slice; real name ext4_has_unknown_ext4_incompat_features.

name: ext4_ext_insert_extent
prose: Real function ext4_ext_insert_extent(handle, inode, path, newext, gb_flags) (the slice begins in the middle of it; the packet suffix '(tail; name elided in excerpt)' is not part of the name). Precondition: handle is an active journal handle with enough credits, path is the path returned by ext4_find_extent for the logical block of newext (valid down to the leaf at ext_depth(inode)) and is owned by the caller, newext points to a valid extent to insert whose block range does not overlap an existing extent, and gb_flags holds EXT4_GET_BLOCKS_* flags. Postcondition: returns a struct ext4_ext_path * or an ERR_PTR. On success the returned path (which may be a different path from the one passed in: the old one is then freed, e.g. when the next leaf or a newly created leaf is used) is owned by the caller, and newext has been merged with an adjacent extent (unless gb_flags has EXT4_GET_BLOCKS_PRE_IO, which skips merging) or inserted in sorted position in the leaf, eh_entries incremented, the indexes above corrected and the leaf buffer marked dirty (ext4_ext_dirty). On failure it returns ERR_PTR(err) and the caller must not use or free the path it passed in: -EFSCORRUPTED if newext has actual length 0 or path[depth].p_hdr is NULL (after EXT4_ERROR_INODE), or the error of ext4_ext_get_access, ext4_find_extent (looking for the next leaf), ext4_ext_create_new_leaf (e.g. -ENOSPC; it returns the error path itself), ext4_ext_correct_indexes or ext4_ext_dirty; except that for the create-new-leaf failure the path is as released by that function. The in-memory extent leaf may already have been modified when a late step (index correction or dirtying) fails.
note: Slice head cut; real name ext4_ext_insert_extent. Removed the unsupported 'tree left consistent' claim and made path ownership on both outcomes explicit.

name: ext4_es_lookup_extent
prose: Real function ext4_es_lookup_extent(inode, lblk, next_lblk, es) (slice head cut). Precondition: inode is a valid ext4 inode, es points to writable struct extent_status storage, next_lblk is NULL or points to a writable ext4_lblk_t, and the caller does not hold EXT4_I(inode)->i_es_lock. Postcondition: returns 0 immediately, leaving es and *next_lblk untouched, if the filesystem is in fast-commit replay (s_mount_state & EXT4_FC_REPLAY). Otherwise it takes i_es_lock for reading (released before return), first zeroes es->es_lblk, es_len and es_pblk, then looks for an extent containing lblk (first the cached tree->cache_es, then the rb-tree). If found it returns 1 with es filled from that extent (es_lblk, es_len, es_pblk), marks the tree's extent as referenced (the flag is set even under the read lock), increments the cache-hit statistic, and, if next_lblk is non-NULL, sets *next_lblk to the es_lblk of the next extent in the tree or to 0 if there is none. If not found it returns 0 with es zeroed (all three fields 0), *next_lblk unchanged and the cache-miss statistic incremented.
note: Fixed: es is zeroed on a miss (previous prose said unmodified); FC_REPLAY early return; referenced flag set on hit.

name: ext4_fc_value_len_isvalid
prose: Precondition: sbi points to a valid ext4_sb_info (only sbi->s_inode_size is read, for the inode-tag case); tag and len are the tag value and the payload length (fc_len) read from a fast-commit tag-length record. No locks are needed. Postcondition: returns true exactly when the length is valid for the tag: for EXT4_FC_TAG_ADD_RANGE (1) len == sizeof(struct ext4_fc_add_range) = 16; EXT4_FC_TAG_DEL_RANGE (2) len == sizeof(struct ext4_fc_del_range) = 12; EXT4_FC_TAG_CREAT, LINK and UNLINK (3, 4, 5) len - sizeof(struct ext4_fc_dentry_info) (8) lies in [1, EXT4_NAME_LEN (255)] (the name length); EXT4_FC_TAG_INODE (6) len - sizeof(struct ext4_fc_inode) (4) lies in [EXT4_GOOD_OLD_INODE_SIZE (128), sbi->s_inode_size]; EXT4_FC_TAG_PAD (7) any len; EXT4_FC_TAG_TAIL (8) len >= sizeof(struct ext4_fc_tail) = 8; EXT4_FC_TAG_HEAD (9) len == sizeof(struct ext4_fc_head) = 8. Any other tag returns false. Pure: no memory, lock or reference effects.
note: Fixed constants: tags ADD_RANGE=1 .. HEAD=9, DEL_RANGE size 12, HEAD size 8, dentry info 8; no contract because the INODE bound reads sbi->s_inode_size.

name: ext4_fc_replay
prose: Precondition: called by jbd2 (journal->j_private is the ext4 super_block) as the fast-commit replay callback for one fast-commit block: bh holds the block data (journal->j_blocksize bytes), pass is PASS_SCAN or a later replay pass, off the block's offset, expected_tid the expected transaction id; the caller serialises replay. Postcondition: for PASS_SCAN it sets sbi->s_fc_replay_state.fc_current_pass = PASS_SCAN and returns ext4_fc_replay_scan(journal, bh, off, expected_tid). For any other pass, if fc_current_pass differs from pass it sets fc_current_pass = pass and sets EXT4_FC_REPLAY in sbi->s_mount_state. If fc_replay_num_tags is 0 it calls ext4_fc_set_bitmaps_and_counters(sb) and returns 0. With CONFIG_EXT4_DEBUG, if s_fc_debug_max_replay is non-zero and off >= it, it returns JBD2_FC_REPLAY_STOP at once without replaying any tag or decrementing fc_replay_num_tags. Otherwise it walks the tag-length records in the block: if fc_replay_num_tags is 0 mid-block it calls ext4_fc_set_bitmaps_and_counters and returns JBD2_FC_REPLAY_STOP; otherwise it decrements fc_replay_num_tags and applies the tag (LINK, UNLINK, ADD_RANGE, CREAT, DEL_RANGE, INODE through the matching ext4_fc_replay_* helper; PAD and HEAD do nothing; TAIL warns if its tid differs from expected_tid; any unknown tag gives -ECANCELED). A negative result stops the walk and is returned (with fc_replay_num_tags already decremented for the failing tag); otherwise it returns JBD2_FC_REPLAY_CONTINUE after the last tag in the block (also when the block holds no complete tag).
note: Fixed per rounds 1-2: PASS_SCAN updates fc_current_pass; debug max_replay path returns STOP without replaying; documented the TAIL warning and unknown-tag -ECANCELED.

name: ext4_fc_mark_ineligible
prose: Precondition: sb is a valid ext4 super_block, reason is a EXT4_FC_REASON_* value less than EXT4_FC_REASON_MAX (WARN_ON otherwise, and the statistics array would be indexed out of range), handle is NULL, an error pointer, or a valid journal handle; the caller holds neither the fast-commit lock nor the journal's j_state_lock. Postcondition: returns void. If fast commit is disabled for sb (ext4_fc_disabled) it returns immediately with no effect at all (no flag, no tid, no statistics). Otherwise it determines a transaction id: the handle's transaction tid if handle is valid, else the running transaction's tid read under j_state_lock, or no tid if there is no running transaction. Under the fast-commit lock it then sets EXT4_MF_FC_INELIGIBLE (always), and records sbi->s_fc_ineligible_tid = tid only when a tid was obtained and either the filesystem was not already marked ineligible or tid is newer than the recorded one; when no tid was obtained, or the existing recorded tid is not older, s_fc_ineligible_tid is left unchanged. After dropping the lock it increments the per-reason ineligible counter sbi->s_fc_stats.fc_ineligible_reason_count[reason]. No references are taken.
note: Fixed: early return when fast commit is disabled; tid update only if a transaction tid exists and condition holds; counter incremented after unlock.

name: ext4_mark_bitmap_end
prose: Precondition: start_bit and end_bit are non-negative ints and bitmap points to a writable bitmap with room for bit index end_bit - 1 (and for bit index ceil8(start_bit) - 1 when start_bit is not a multiple of 8, which may lie beyond end_bit - 1). Postcondition: returns void; the bitmap is unchanged if start_bit >= end_bit. Otherwise, with b = the smallest multiple of 8 that is >= start_bit: every bit in [start_bit, b) is set to 1 (empty when start_bit is a multiple of 8; the range may extend past end_bit, e.g. start_bit 5 and end_bit 6 sets bits 5, 6 and 7), and if b < end_bit every whole byte of the bitmap from byte b/8 up to the byte before end_bit's byte (i.e. the bits [b, end_bit rounded down to a multiple of 8)) is set to 0xff; all bits outside these ranges, including a trailing partial byte up to end_bit - 1, are left unmodified. No lock, reference or allocation is involved.
note: Fixed per round-2: first range is empty when start_bit is a multiple of 8 (boundary is the smallest multiple of 8 >= start_bit); second range described as whole bytes up to end_bit rounded down.
